approach.label: Approach
approach.title: How a question becomes a thing.
approach.note: Five steps, in this order. The last one leads back to the first.

steps.title: Observe
steps.text: See what people do, not what they say they do.

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: Find the real question under the request.

steps.title: Experiment
steps.text: Build the smallest thing that could prove me wrong.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Turn what survived into something people can use.

steps.title: Improve
steps.text: Ship, watch, adjust. Then look again.

home.greeting: Hi, I'm the cat. I know a few things about Iury. What would you like to know?

chips.label: Who is Iury?
chips.answer: An IT Assistant at Giassi Supermercados, working with SQL, PL/SQL and Oracle. He studies Computer Science (UNESC) and Systems Analysis and Development (UNOPAR). He learns by building, and this site shows what he found.

chips.label: AI experience?
chips.answer: The fullest case is Koinonia, a live product built with AI. Iury defined the problem, wrote the directives, ran the build and tested the result. At work he uses AI to write rules and automations on the DOX platform.

chips.label: How to reach him?
chips.answer: By email, iuryumbelino1@gmail.com, or on LinkedIn (in/iuryumbelino). His GitHub is @Umbelino-dev. Taking you to the contact section.

home.fallback: I'm still a prototype. My answers are scripted, with no language model behind them. Try one of the suggestions.

koinonia.greeting: I've read this case study. Ask me why a Radar, how AI was used or what the audit found.

chips.label: Why a Radar?
chips.answer: Because an attendance list says who came, not where to start. The Radar ranks people by risk of drifting away and turns that into a care queue. Newcomers are not flagged as at risk.

chips.label: How was AI used?
chips.answer: AI wrote the code from a brief and plans Iury wrote. He directed every round, checked the result and tested it on desktop and mobile.

chips.label: What did the audit find?
chips.answer: Silent failures. Unpaginated reads would have broken the Radar past a thousand records. An inverted date filter hid people who needed care. And there were no tests. All fixed.

koinonia.fallback: About this project I can only answer the suggestions above. I'm still a scripted prototype.
